chapter: Band personalities, Duke's last years and the office
title: Puerto Rican independence and crime
summary: He opposes independence and says it is dangerous out after eight in San Juan.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: He is Cuban, but now he don't want to, because he's trying to file -- in Puerto Rico, they want to be independent, you know? Some group wants Puerto Rico to be independent, which I don't like, because the first time I hear that Puerto Rico goes independent, I'm going to go downtown and tell them I am still an American citizen; I don't want no independence. Because it is just too small, you know? Too small to be independent. That's part of some Communists working in there; the politics is awful in Puerto Rico. Very bad.

And still, when I was over there, you can get out at night after eight o'clock, you're liable to be held up, or do something, so I never did go out after eight. After eight o'clock, I was in the hotel.
Just like everywhere else, you know?
Yeah. I don't know anyplace where it's not like that.
Oh, they break in your house, or do something or other.
